questions.stem: In the question below, three sentences are given which may not be in grammatically correct form. Choose the set of sentence(s) from the given options that is/are incorrect. If all the sentences are correct, choose “No Error” as the answer choice. (A) The committee, which comprises experts from diverse fields, have been deliberating for weeks but has yet to arrive at a unanimous decision. (B) She insisted that the final draft be reviewed thoroughly before it is sent to the publisher for approval. (C) The traditions of the region, which date back several centuries, continues to influence the lifestyle of people even today.
questions.explanation: Sentence (A) Original: The committee, which comprises experts from diverse fields, have been deliberating for weeks but has yet to arrive at a unanimous decision. Error: Subject–verb disagreement Rule: A collective noun (committee, team, jury, crowd) is treated as singular when the group acts as a single unit. Therefore, the verb must be singular. • “The committee … has been deliberating” → correct • “The committee … have been deliberating” → incorrect here Correct sentence: The committee, which comprises experts from diverse fields, has been deliberating for weeks but has yet to arrive at a unanimous decision. Example: The jury are giving its verdict. (incorrect) The jury is giving its verdict. → (A) contains an error. Sentence (B) Original: She insisted that the final draft be reviewed thoroughly before it is sent to the publisher for approval. Error: No error. Rule: After verbs expressing suggestion, demand, insistence, recommendation (such as insist, suggest, recommend, demand, propose), the subjunctive mood is used. Structure: subject + verb + that + subject + base verb Here: • "She insisted that the draft be reviewed" → correct subjunctive use. Example: The teacher recommended that he submit the form today. → (B) is correct. Sentence (C) Original: The traditions of the region, which date back several centuries, continues to influence the lifestyle of people even today. Error: Subject–verb disagreement Rule: The verb agrees with the main subject, not the phrase in between. Main subject: The traditions (plural) Verb should be continue, not continues. Correct sentence: The traditions of the region, which date back several centuries, continue to influence the lifestyle of people even today. Example: The books on the shelf belong to Riya. (Not: belongs) → (C) contains an error. Correct option: (d) Only (A) and (C)

questions.stem: In the question below, three sentences are given which may not be in grammatically correct form. Choose the set of sentence(s) from the given options that is/are incorrect. If all the sentences are correct, choose “No Error” as the answer choice. (A) The findings of the report indicates that several crucial policies were implemented without assessing their long-term impact on rural livelihoods. (B) No sooner had the announcement been made than the investors began to reconsider their earlier decisions. (C) Each of the participants who were shortlisted for the final round were required to submit an additional set of documents.
questions.explanation: Sentence (A) Original: The findings of the report indicates that several crucial policies were implemented without assessing their long-term impact on rural livelihoods. Error: Subject–verb disagreement Rule: Verb must agree with the head noun of the subject. Here, the subject is findings (plural), not report. • Findings indicate (plural verb) Correct sentence: The findings of the report indicate that several crucial policies were implemented… Example: The results of the study shows improvement. (incorrect) The results of the study show improvement. → (A) contains an error. Sentence (B) Original: No sooner had the announcement been made than the investors began to reconsider their earlier decisions. Error: No error. Rule: The correlative pair No sooner… than requires inversion (helping verb before subject). Correct structure: No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than + main clause This sentence follows the rule perfectly. Example: No sooner had he arrived than it started raining. → (B) is correct. Sentence (C) Original: Each of the participants who were shortlisted for the final round were required to submit an additional set of documents. Errors: 1. Subject–verb disagreement with "Each" 2. Pronoun–verb mismatch in the relative clause Rule 1 — “Each” is always singular. So the main verb must be singular: Each … was required Rule 2 — The relative pronoun “who” should refer to the noun closest to it. Here, “who” refers to participants (plural), so “were shortlisted” is correct. Correct structure: • "Each … was required" (singular) • "participants who were shortlisted" (plural) Correct sentence: Each of the participants who were shortlisted for the final round was required to submit an additional set of documents. Example: Each of the applicants was given a separate form. → (C) contains an error. Correct option (b) Both (A) and (C)

questions.direction_text: Read the following passage and answer the given questions. What may seem like an innocuous television commercial or a playful Instagram post can, in reality, be a calculated attempt at psychological persuasion. Deceptive advertising has become increasingly sophisticated, employing techniques that blur the line between suggestion and manipulation. While not always overtly fraudulent, many of these practices are ethically questionable and, in some cases, egregious. A recent study conducted by Stanford University revealed that emotionally resonant advertisements significantly increase consumer trust, even when the claims lack empirical evidence. The research found that people under stress or time constraints were especially vulnerable, responding more positively to emotionally charged ads that appeal to sentiment rather than logic. Adding to this concern, a joint investigation by the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Cambridge examined the growing trend of hyper-targeted digital ads. These ads, often powered by AI algorithms, utilize personal browsing histories to present consumers with content tailored to their psychological profiles. The findings suggest that such ads are not only invasive but also exploitative, particularly when they use ambiguous or scientific-sounding terms like "clinically tested" or "dermatologist approved" that lack standardized definitions. Especially troubling is the targeting of vulnerable demographics—including teenagers, the elderly, and low-income communities—who may lack the critical thinking skills or access to reliable information necessary to evaluate claims. The Cambridge study noted a marked decline in skepticism among such groups, making them more susceptible to spurious health products, financial schemes, and false promises. Though regulatory bodies like the Federal Trade Commission exist, enforcement remains patchy and reactive. Loopholes and vague language in advertising codes allow brands to operate in grey zones, maintaining plausible deniability while misleading consumers. As deceptive techniques grow more refined, the need for media literacy, ethical oversight, and clearer legal definitions becomes urgent. Consumers must be equipped not only to recognize manipulative rhetoric, but also to question the intent behind even the most innocuous-seeming promotional content.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: (a) Rules currently exist but are applied unevenly and fail to keep pace with modern tactics. Relevant lines from the passage: • “Though regulatory bodies like the Federal Trade Commission exist, enforcement remains patchy and reactive.” • “Loopholes and vague language in advertising codes allow brands to operate in grey zones…” Explanation of the correct option (a): Option (a) accurately reflects the author’s view. The passage clearly states that while regulatory bodies such as the FTC are in place, the enforcement of rules is inconsistent ("patchy and reactive"). It also highlights that outdated or vague regulations allow deceptive advertising practices to persist. This directly supports the idea that rules exist but are unevenly applied and not keeping up with modern advertising tactics. Why the other options are incorrect: (b) Oversight is consistent and successfully prevents most forms of deceptive advertising. Incorrect — The passage explicitly states that enforcement is inconsistent ("patchy") and ineffective in preventing deceptive practices. (c) Existing guidelines are too strict overall and tend to restrict creative marketing ideas. Incorrect — The author never claims the guidelines are too strict; instead, they argue that the guidelines are too weak, vague, and easily exploited. (d) The federal agency in charge plays a major role in enabling manipulative advertising. Incorrect — The passage criticizes weak enforcement but does not say that the FTC actively enables manipulation. It points to loopholes and vague rules, not intentional enabling. (e) Present legal standards are highly effective and have removed misleading practices. Incorrect — This directly contradicts the passage, which argues that deceptive advertising is still widespread due to ineffective regulation.

questions.stem: The severe water shortage forced the resources to manage its precarious community more carefully to avoid a crisis during an/a increasingly limited period.
questions.direction_text: A sentence is given with five words highlighted in bold. Choose the word that is correct placed at its position.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (d) increasingly “Increasingly” is the only word correctly placed in the sentence. Given Sentence: The severe water shortage forced the resources to manage its precarious community more carefully to avoid a crisis during an/a increasingly limited period. WORD-BY-WORD MEANING, EXAMPLE & PLACEMENT ANALYSIS (a) resources — Incorrect placement Meaning • English: supplies or assets used for support or survival • Hindi: संसाधन, साधन Example (English) The school lacked the resources to upgrade its computers. Why incorrect? “Forced the resources to manage…” is wrong because: • Resources cannot take action. • People or a community manage resources, not the other way around. So “resources” is wrongly placed. (b) limited — Incorrect placement Meaning • English: small in amount; restricted • Hindi: सीनित Example (English) The villagers survived on limited drinking water during the drought. Why incorrect? The phrase “increasingly limited period” is grammatically correct, but in this sentence: • The adjective limited is supposed to describe resources, not period. • The sentence context earlier is incorrect, which makes this word misplaced in the overall structure. Thus “limited” is not correctly placed in this sentence structure. (c) community — Incorrect placement Meaning • English: a group of people living together • Hindi: सिुिाय Example (English) The community united to conserve water during the summer. Why incorrect? The sentence says: • “forced the resources to manage its precarious community” This is incorrect because: • You don’t manage a community in this context. • You manage resources, not “a precarious community.” • Also, “resources” cannot have a community (“its community”). Therefore, “community” is incorrectly placed. (d) increasingly — Correct placement Meaning • English: more and more; progressively • Hindi: बढ़ते हुए रूप से / लगातार अनधक Example (English) The weather has become increasingly unpredictable. Why correct? It correctly modifies an adjective: • increasingly limited period Here, “increasingly” shows that the period is becoming more and more limited. Its grammatical placement and meaning are accurate, making it the only correctly placed word. (e) precarious — Incorrect placement Meaning • English: risky, unstable, insecure • Hindi: अनस्िर, अनननित, जोनखिपूण Example (English) They lived in a precarious situation after the landslide. Why incorrect? The sentence uses: • “to manage its precarious community” This is incorrect because: • A community is not usually described as “precarious.” • Precarious describes situations, conditions, or positions, not a group of people. • The correct phrase in context should have been something like “precarious period”. Hence, “precarious” is incorrectly placed. Final Answer: (d) increasingly It is the only word that is grammatically, logically, and contextually correct at its position.
